question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{-(x+y)}, & x\ge 0,\,y\ge 0, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

The marginal CDF ${F}_{X}(x)$ of $X$ is given by

$$
{F}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<0 \\ g(x), & x\ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

What is the function $g(x)?$

Find the marginal cumulative distribution function (CDF) $F_Y(y)$ of $Y.$
current_example.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x, y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, the marginal density function of $Y$ for $-1 \leq y \leq 1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{3}{8}(x+y)^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{8}{[\frac{1}{3}(x+y)^{3}]}_{x=-1}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}{[(x+y)^{3}]}_{x=-1}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}[(1+y)^{3}-(-1+y)^{3}] \\  & =\frac{1}{8}[(y+1)^{3}-(y-1)^{3}] \\  & =\frac{1}{8}[({y}^{3}+3{y}^{2}+3y+1)-({y}^{3}-3{y}^{2}+3y-1)] \\  & =\frac{1}{8}[(\cancel{{y}^{3}}+3{y}^{2}+\cancel{3y}+1)-(\cancel{{y}^{3}}-3{y}^{2}+\cancel{3y}-1)] \\  & =\frac{1}{8}[2(3{y}^{2}+1)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(3{y}^{2}+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the marginal CDF of $Y$ for $-1 \leq y \leq 1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{y}{f}_{Y}(u)\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{y}\frac{1}{4}(3{u}^{2}+1)\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{-1}^{y}(3{u}^{2}+1)\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{[{u}^{3}+u]}_{-1}^{y} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[{y}^{3}+y-(-1)^{3}-(-1)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[{y}^{3}+y+2] \\  & =\frac{{y}^{3}+y+2}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for the marginal CDF of $Y$ is
